summary: Two synthesis-only experiments completed in 0.2 reconstructed minutes, with no compute-bound experiments. The GPU snapshot therefore does not establish a compute-task idle fault, and no concurrent-model DualGPURunner requirement applied.
bottlenecks_identified: Timing observability was the only identifiable limitation: disk-mtime reconstruction replaced live commit timing and exposed no task-phase attribution.
No execution bottleneck was established because both completed experiments were synthesis-only and no compute-bound work existed for GPU or runner diagnosis.
improvements_suggested: Persist monotonic task-start, task-end, and phase timestamps in each experiment artifact so retrospective timing does not depend on disk modification times or milestone commits.
Record task-scoped workload class, model count, GPU samples, and runner choice, while marking compute dispatch fields not applicable for synthesis-only work.
Surface an observability warning whenever the live git-log timing path contains no milestone commits and fallback reconstruction is used.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add monotonic task and phase timing receipts to every experiment artifact.
Attach workload-class, model-count, GPU, and runner metadata to the task that produced each timing row.
Flag zero-commit timing windows and retain explicit fallback provenance in the retrospective input.
meta_reflection: GPU utilization and DualGPURunner are not valid optimization targets for this synthesis-only closeout. Task-linked timing must improve before the evidence can support a nonzero speedup estimate.
